transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood), Jamal Singh (Redwood SE), Lina Chen (Redwood Product), Mark Reynolds (NovaSearch CTO), Priya Kapoor (NovaSearch ML Eng), Tom Hargreaves (NovaSearch Platform)

Summary:
Quick migration/demo walkthrough focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood API, console overview (observability + routing), and Redwood Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. Customer wants a clear migration path, sample snippets, and initial POC to verify latency and cost.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh we'll kick off at 3.00. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE on the account. Jamal and Lina are with me. How's it going Mark?
[00:08] Mark: Hey Ava, good thanks. We're excited. We run a search product, NovaSearch, lots of embeddings + chat assistants, trying to move away from vendor lock with OpenAI and a couple Anthropic endpoints.
[00:16] Ava: Perfect. The goal today is a migration demo - parity mapping - show how your existing calls map to Redwood, show console/optimize, and outline POC next steps. Jamal, do you want to start with API mapping?
[00:25] Jamal: Sure. I'll share my screen - bear with me if the screen share hiccups. So first principle: Redwood exposes a single unified API for text, chat, embeddings and reranking. For customers using OpenAI Chat Completions, we map chat -> Redwood chat endpoints, the payload differences are small: messages array, role/content, function-calling semantics are supported but note slight differences in function call naming and 'response_format' flags.
[00:45] Priya: Quick q - do you keep same token counting? We bill per-token but we want to make sure our cost calc maps to what we see from OpenAI.
[00:52] Jamal: Good call. Redwood tokenization and billing is aligned with common tokenizers; for parity we provide a tokenizer tool in the console and the SDK to estimate tokens. There may be small diffs in how stop sequences or special tokens are handled, but we include a token-diff report in the parity spreadsheet we'll send.
[01:10] Mark: And embeddings? We use OpenAI embeddings heavily - 4M requests a month. Latency matters for online similarity.
[01:17] Jamal: Embeddings map directly - same shape: input -> vector. We have a one-to-one mapping for the popular OpenAI and Anthropic models to Redwood-verified equivalents; you can call Redwood embeddings endpoint exactly like you call an OpenAI one, examples we'll share: curl + python. There are options to pin model versions, and also a batching endpoint to improve throughput.
[01:36] Tom: Is streaming supported? For our chat UI we use streaming tokens from OpenAI.
[01:40] Jamal: Yes - Redwood supports SSE + Websocket streaming for chat. The SDKs expose an identical stream interface; the only nuance is that we include an optional prefix cache header to reduce cost on repeated prompts.
[01:52] [01:52] Lina: I'll jump in and show the console briefly - it's important for your platform folks.
[01:56] [02:00] Lina: (screen) Console -> Projects -> NovaSearch demo. Here you see per-route latency, token breakdown, and rollouts. You can pin model variants, set fallback policies - e.g., route to a cheaper quantized variant when latency budget permits. I want to call out Optimize: it will recommend batching/kv cache settings based on traffic patterns.
[02:22] Priya: That kv cache - is that the same as a prefix cache? Does it persist between requests for different sessions?
[02:28] Lina: Good nuance. The KV cache we mean is per-session KV for decoder-only models, mainly to speed up long-context chats. Prefix caching is different - we cache common prefixes across requests to save compute. Both are configurable; Optimize will suggest thresholds.
[02:45] Mark: Security/compliance - we need SOC2 docs and SSO/SAML, and customer-managed KMS for keys.
[02:52] Ava: Absolutely, we have SOC2 and ISO docs, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated deployments. For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption and enterprise KMS options. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[03:10] Tom: If we go Dedicated, how does networking work? We have strict egress rules and need VPC peering.
[03:16] Jamal: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For on-prem it's more involved but doable; we'll capture your network constraints in the action items.
[03:25] [03:30] Priya: On the technical parity - function calling is a blocker for a subset of our agents. OpenAI's function calling is used to surface structured responses. How do you map that?
[03:36] Jamal: Redwood supports function/tool calling semantics - payloads are similar. Differences: we use 'tools' object and a 'tool_call' hint; we'll include a one-to-one mapping sample. There are edgecases with multi-step tool calls where Anthropic's approach differs, but we have transformation helpers in the SDK to normalise.
[03:56] Priya: Ok good. Also, what about rate limits and error modes? We sometimes get 429s and retry logic is embedded in our clients.
[04:03] Jamal: We expose rate limit headers and a recommended retry/backoff in the SDK. For Dedicated you can get predictable throughput commitments so you rarely see 429s. For hosted we provide quota windows and burst options.
[04:18] Mark: Can you run a quick demo of taking a small OpenAI chat request and hitting Redwood?
[04:22] Jamal: Yup. I have a snippet. (shares terminal) Here's an OpenAI-like curl: 
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize product usage"}]}'

On Redwood it's: 
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize product usage"}], "model":"redwood-4o"}'

You'll notice the body is similar, model names change and the endpoint path is unified. We'll include full replacements for function syntax.
[05:05] Priya: Any SDK differences? We use the OpenAI python SDK currently.
[05:09] Jamal: We provide drop-in SDKs with similar call signatures; in python the call shape is nearly identical. We'll include a side-by-side doc for your engineers. There's a small change for how we return streaming chunks (we include metadata fields) - it's painless but worth testing.
[05:23] Mark: How about Anthropic -> Redwood mapping? Some of our safety configs run in Anthropic.
[05:27] Jamal: Anthropic 'system' vs 'user' mapping does vary. For safety configs we support per-request safety flags, and the console has policy overrides. For parity we'll list recommended equivalent flags and any behavioral diffs in the sheet.
[05:46] Tom: Performance - do you have representative latency numbers for embeddings compared to OpenAI?
[05:49] Lina: We publish verified performance profiles per model in the catalog. For many open models we see comparable or better p50/p95 on the same GPU class due to optimized kernels and KV cache. But the big lever is batching + quantization for throughput. We'll run a short benchmark in the POC on your workloads.
[06:10] Priya: Cost perspective - we need to understand per-token cost and also how quantized variants affect quality.
[06:15] Lina: Optimize helps there. It suggests quantization profiles and estimates quality delta; we can run evals on your prompt sets and surface BLEU/ROUGE or our custom quality metrics. For the migration we recommend starting with hosted to validate parity, then move to Dedicated if throughput/cost needs dictate.
[06:34] [06:40] Mark: Anything we should be worried about? Like reranking differences?
[06:44] Jamal: Reranking is supported; if you currently do synchronous rerank calls we can recommend batching or a hybrid pipeline. There are small ordering differences sometimes because of float ops between providers; not usually material but we'll capture that in the parity tests.
[06:58] Priya: Can you show the console's token estimator?
[07:00] Lina: Sure - (screen) Token estimator, paste prompts, it'll show estimated tokens and cost delta between model variants. You can run a bulk token report by uploading CSV. That helps with that 4M embeddings/month guess.
[07:18] Tom: For the POC benchmarks, what infra do you need from our side?
[07:22] Jamal: For hosted POC, we just need sample prompt sets, keys, and a representative test harness. For Dedicated/Private POC we'll need network setup and potentially a small dataset. We'll draft a runner to send per-route traffic and record p50/p95, throughput, and cost.
[07:42] Mark: Timeline - we'd like to make a decision within 3 weeks if POC looks good.
[07:46] Ava: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to send artifacts in 48 hours and start a POC next week.
[07:51] [08:00] Priya: One more technical: does Redwood support chat multi-turn with long contexts (50k tokens)? We have some agents that do long-context retrieval augmented generation.
[08:08] Jamal: Yes - long context is supported with our KV cache and long context model families. For very long contexts we recommend sharding + prefix caching. There are some memory/latency tradeoffs we'll show in Optimize suggestions.
[08:24] Mark: Any gotchas about prompt formatting? We use a mix of raw text and JSON for structured outputs.
[08:30] Jamal: We support structured outputs via response_format and function calling; JSON outputs can be enforced with schema validators in the console. Sometimes tokenization differences require small prompt tweaks but nothing big.
[08:44] [08:50] Ava: Ok let's recap real quick - action items and next steps. Ava: We'll send the parity mapping spreadsheet containing endpoint mappings, model equivalences, and sample curl/python snippets (Ava). Jamal: he'll prepare a small POC runner and run an initial latency test. Priya: share prompt sets and token volumes. Tom: share network constraints. We'll schedule the POC kickoff next week. Anything to add?
[09:10] Mark: Please include Dedicated pricing options in the email.
[09:14] Ava: Will do. We'll also attach SOC2 and SSO docs.
[09:20] Priya: Thanks - one small note, our legal team will want data retention and deletion language up front.
[09:24] Ava: We'll include that in the security pack.
[09:28] Lina: Quick note - I also linked an internal demo repo and a spreadsheet with model performance comparisons in the chat. Links: [redwood.com/demo-repo] [drive/pricing-sheet].
[09:38] Tom: Great, thanks everyone.

(brief crosstalk)

[09:45] Ava: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:50] End of recording.

Call Notes / Artifacts Shared:

End.
